newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline sharpens losses late with crude.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline sharpens losses late with crude.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline's sharp losses accelerated Wednesday afternoon while crude tested new session lows following data which showed burgeoning supply in both.
At 1347 EDT, June gasoline was off 1.86 cents at 62.90 cents a gallon, after falling to new session low of 62.75, which was about 0.50 cent lower than this morning's low.
June crude stood 45 cents a barrel lower at $20.92 after breaking the ACCESS low of $20.88, a minor support level held early session.
"The only reason we were holding above 63.00 cents in gasoline is because crude was holding, when crude started to fall again, so did gasoline," said a New York gasoline trader.
The dealer noted gasoline and crude price movements were linked as their supply fundamentals were deemed equally bearish in oil inventory reports reflecting the week ended May 9.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) said gasoline stocks grew a much larger-than-expected 6.51 million barrels when traders had expected a build of only a one million barrels. Moreover, gasoline production rose to 8.1 million barrels per day (bpd) from 7.8 million bpd.
The Department of Energy (DOE) said in its own weekly data for the same period that gasoline stocks rose 4.7 million barrels.
Gasoline production was spurred on by a sharp rise in refinery run rates that stood at a feverish 96.9 percent versus 94.5 percent last week.

Despite the high run rates and lower imports, crude stocks grew 6.94 million barrels compared to a build expected by traders of less than one million barrels. Moreover, the API saidcrude stocks stood 22.9 million barrels above a year ago.
Still, traders were not willing to sound the death knell to prompt crude's new range of $20.50 to $21.50 until it broke through the key $20.50 level of support.
"I don't like crude right now, but you don't get real bearish until it goes back under $20.50," said a New York crude trader.
Distillate stocks, comprised of heating oil and diesel, dropped 1.10 million barrels when dealers had expected a build.
But, heating oil prices followed the rest of the oil complex lower, with June heat off 0.73 cent at 55.75 cents a gallon.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
